name: Hierarchical Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Level Vector Filtering
description: In massive enterprise catalogs, searching 100 million items is accelerated by first matching high-level department embedding centroids, then searching specific item vectors inside matching departments.
prompt:
In massive enterprise catalogs, searching 100 million items is accelerated by first matching high-level department embedding centroids, then searching specific item vectors inside matching departments.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: item_id, item_name, fine_sim_score.
Results should be ordered as specified.
golden_sql:
-- Find best matching department, then retrieve top items strictly within that department
            WITH top_dept AS (
                SELECT dept_id
                FROM departments
                ORDER BY array_cosine_similarity(dept_centroid, [0.95, 0.05]::FLOAT[2]) DESC
                LIMIT 1
            )
            SELECT 
                i.item_id,
                i.item_name,
                ROUND(array_cosine_similarity(i.item_vector, [0.95, 0.05]::FLOAT[2]), 4) AS fine_sim_score
            FROM items i
            JOIN top_dept d ON i.dept_id = d.dept_id
            ORDER BY fine_sim_score DESC;
why_it_fails: Flat brute-force vector search over hundreds of millions of items consumes excessive compute.
